title: NEB Class 12 Chemistry — Hydrocarbons — 2024
subject: chemistry
source: NEB Grade 12 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: State Markovnikov's rule and explain it on the basis of the carbocation mechanism; also state the peroxide (Kharasch) effect.
questions.solution:
**Markovnikov's rule:** in the addition of HX to an unsymmetrical alkene, the negative part goes to the carbon carrying the smaller number of hydrogens.

**Reason:** the first step is protonation of the double bond, and the more stable carbocation decides the product. Addition of H⁺ to propene gives CH₃CH⁺CH₃ (2°, more stable) rather than CH₃CH₂CH₂⁺ (1°), so Br⁻ attaches to C-2 and the product is 2-bromopropane.

**Peroxide effect:** with peroxides the mechanism becomes free-radical, giving the anti-Markovnikov product (1-bromopropane) because the more stable secondary radical forms.
questions.knowledgeNote: Only HBr shows the peroxide effect; HCl and HI add by the ionic path regardless, since their radical steps are unfavourable.

questions.question: Write the reactions of benzene with (a) conc. HNO₃/H₂SO₄, (b) Cl₂/FeCl₃, (c) CH₃Cl/anhydrous AlCl₃, and name the type of mechanism involved.
questions.knowledgeNote: Benzene prefers substitution to addition precisely because addition would destroy its aromatic stabilisation (about 150 kJ mol⁻¹).

questions.question: How will you distinguish between ethane, ethene and ethyne using simple chemical tests?
questions.solution:
- **Bromine water:** decolourised by ethene and ethyne (addition), unchanged by ethane.
- **Ammoniacal AgNO₃ or Cu₂Cl₂:** a white (Ag) or red-brown (Cu) precipitate identifies ethyne (terminal ≡CH, acidic hydrogen); ethene gives no precipitate.
- **Alkaline KMnO₄ (Baeyer's reagent):** decolourised by both unsaturated gases, giving a diol — confirms unsaturation while distinguishing them from ethane.
questions.knowledgeNote: Terminal alkynes are acidic because the sp-carbon holds the electron pair tightly — the basis of the silver/copper acetylide tests.
